why: The program lists an article as basic reading, but it does not directly cover the ADPF 153–Gomes Lund question on international duties; no basic-reading chapter fits this case-centered eixo.

Official STF ementa/acórdão (PDF pp. 1–4) identifies the ADPF and summarizes the majority’s treatment of Lei 6.683/79, the breadth and historical setting of the amnesty, and the invoked international torture norms; it supplies the mapped case’s holding and stated grounds.

Use the relator’s vote at §§ 25–29 for the meaning of connected crimes and bilateral amnesty, §§ 42–43 for the timing and domestic reach of international instruments, and §§ 46–47 for institutional authority to revise the amnesty; these are the majority grounds directly tested by the eixo.

Use vote sections 3–8 (PDF pp. 106–130), especially §§ 7–8, where the dissent addresses access to jurisdiction, the ICCPR/Corte IDH duty to investigate, prosecute and punish, and its narrower reading of the amnesty; this gives the mapped legal divergence and disposition.

Use the separate vote’s discussion of the scope of Lei 6.683/79 and its conclusion (PDF pp. 140–146): Ayres Britto would exclude crimes in CF art. 5º, XLIII from the amnesty, a distinct dissent the mapped comparison must identify.
The official plenary record (PDF pp. 265–266) states the ADPF’s final result and names the two dissenting positions, fixing the holding and vote division required by the mapped outcome.
The statute’s art. 1º defines the amnesty’s beneficiaries and temporal scope; that exact article is the legal text interpreted in ADPF 153 and compared with the Corte IDH’s treatment of the same law.

In this 24/08 deck, PDF slides 30–58 move from the transitional-justice balance to the Brazilian ADPF 153 segment, including the OAB claim, truth-and-memory argument, majority account and vote contrast; these slides support the lesson’s mapped Brazil case.
